instruction: Run a network speed test on speedtest.net to assess my current internet connection. Copy the test results shown on speedtest.net/results and save them to the file ~/Test/Speed/results.txt (create the directory structure if needed). Use the format where each metric appears on a new line with the metric name and value separated by a single space.

metadata.explanation: Task involves executing a speed test on speedtest.net, obtaining results from speedtest.net/results page, and writing to a file. Evaluator validates that the saved file includes the three critical network metrics: Ping, Download, and Upload. This is a paraphrase of the original instruction.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification: Evaluator only checks for presence of metric names ('Ping', 'Download', 'Upload') using substring matching, but does not verify the instruction's format requirements

Missing format validation: Instruction explicitly requires 'each metric appears on a new line with the metric name and value separated by a single space', but evaluator does not validate this structure
No value presence check: Evaluator does not verify that actual numeric values are present after the metric names
Overly permissive: A file containing just 'Ping Download Upload' anywhere (even on a single line without values) would pass, violating the instruction's requirements
The file_contains metric (general.py:554-568) only performs substring matching with 'if text not in file_text', not structured format checking
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace file_contains with check_list metric to use regex patterns that verify format: e.g., 'Ping\s+\d+', 'Download\s+[\d.]+', 'Upload\s+[\d.]+'
Use check_list with regex patterns that verify each metric appears on its own line with a numeric value
Alternative: Create a custom getter/metric combination that parses the file line-by-line and validates both the format and presence of numeric values
